subject_line: Wisconsin and Wales side by side in You, Me and the Birds
email_body:
Dear Alan,

I've been reading about You, Me and the Birds, your Parthian collection that sets American and Welsh places alongside each other, with Tony Goble's paintings woven through and a lover re-imagined as a listed building. As a Wisconsin-born poet living in Swansea, I'd love to ask how the two landscapes came to share one book, and how the conversation with Goble's paintings shaped the poems.

subject_line: Tri llais o'r Holocost yn Eira Llwyd
email_body:
Annwyl Gareth,

Rwyf wedi bod yn darllen am Eira Llwyd, eich nofel gyntaf gyda Gwasg y Bwthyn, sy'n dilyn tri pherson Iddewig drwy erchyllterau'r Holocost, ac a ddaeth yn agos i'r brig yng nghystadleuaeth y Fedal Ryddiaith yn 2017. Hoffwn ofyn sut y daethoch i ysgrifennu am y cyfnod hwnnw yn Gymraeg, a sut mae'r gwaith hwnnw'n cysylltu â'ch dramâu a'ch nofel ddiweddarach, Y Cylch.

Prosiect annibynnol yw The Author Ledger sy'n cyhoeddi portreadau byr o awduron. Caiff y portread ei ddatblygu drwy ychydig o gwestiynau ysgrifenedig y gallwch eu hateb yn eich amser eich hun, a rhennir y testun llawn gyda chi i'w adolygu cyn ei gyhoeddi.

A fyddai gennych ddiddordeb mewn cymryd rhan? Dim pwysau o gwbl.

Cofion gorau,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Debut novel Eira Llwyd (Gwasg y Bwthyn 2018) follows three Jews in the Holocaust; near top of 2017 Prose Medal; second novel Y Cylch 2023 (Bangor news). Email seen in search result on Bangor staff page.

subject_line: Migration across three countries in Stretto
email_body:
Dear David,

I came across Stretto, your novel from CB Editions, which follows migration across Ireland, England and Scotland over some twenty years and draws on Joyce and Beckett. As a poet's novel, its musical title caught my attention. I'd be curious to ask how the idea of a stretto, voices overlapping before the last one finishes, shaped the way you built the novel.

subject_line: Leading Lipizzaners over the mountains in Flight
email_body:
Dear Vanessa,

I've been reading about Flight, your Firefly Press novel set in Austria in 1945, where Jakob and the Spanish Riding School groom Herr Engel hide Lipizzaner stallions the Nazis want to seize, and then, with Kizzy, guide them across the mountains. I'd love to ask how you approached writing the horses themselves, and what it was like bringing Kizzy's perspective as a Roma girl into that wartime journey.

subject_line: Johanna's voice in Mrs Van Gogh
email_body:
Dear Caroline,

I've been reading about Mrs Van Gogh, your novel giving voice to Johanna Van Gogh-Bonger, the sister-in-law who kept Vincent's paintings, sketches and letters, and about Daughter of the Titanic, which follows Captain Smith's daughter Helen alongside a later Oxford academic. I'd love to ask how you find these women, and how your earlier experimental fiction as Caroline Smailes shapes the way you write them.

subject_line: Travel and fiction in A Lady Cyclist's Guide to Kashgar
email_body:
Dear Suzanne,

I've been reading about A Lady Cyclist's Guide to Kashgar, your debut novel and a Guardian/Observer Book of the Year in 2012, and about how your own travels have fed into your writing. Since then you've also written a memoir and a second novel. I'd like to ask how the experience of travel turns into fiction for you, and how that has changed from the first novel to the memoir.
